body.x: Safeway Inc. (CEO Dongho Kim) participated in CES 2026 Unveiled, held on January 4 (local time) in Las Vegas, the United States.

Safeway is a Korean company that has developed technologies to address long-standing limitations of commercialized robots and unmanned mobility systems, including obstacles, steps, and rough-terrain mobility. Through continuous development and accumulation of proprietary technologies, the company achieved tangible results by combining adaptive elastic wheel structures with AI-based control technologies.

Between 2024 and 2025, Safeway recorded cumulative domestic sales exceeding 1 billion won, laying the foundation for the commercialization of its technology. The company is currently conducting joint development and demand-linked R&D projects with the Korea Expressway Corporation on traffic signal robots, while also expanding its domestic and overseas business footprint through exports and technical cooperation with electric wheelchair manufacturers.
At CES Unveiled, Safeway introduced the modular mobility solution ‘Ascender,’ which integrates adaptive elastic wheels with AI-driven driving control technology.

The wheel structure of Ascender flexibly deforms in response to obstacles and steps encountered during driving, optimizing ground contact area and propulsion. This enables the platform to overcome heights of up to approximately 1.3 times the wheel radius without relying on complex joint structures or track mechanisms, while maintaining structural simplicity and energy efficiency.

The AI control technology applied to the platform analyzes wheel deformation patterns, ground contact conditions, and motor torque in real time to adjust driving modes accordingly. Through this approach, the company emphasized that Ascender maintains consistent performance on flat surfaces while delivering enhanced stability on irregular terrain, including stairs, curbs, and rough ground. The control system is also designed as a modular solution applicable to various robotic and mobility systems, offering strong scalability.

body.cap: Safeway CEO Dongho Kim is interviewed by AVING News reporter Jay Kennedy Marcus | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Ascender is designed for use across a wide range of applications, including outdoor autonomous robots, electric wheelchairs, and daily living support robots for older adults. Its technological competitiveness and application potential were recognized with an Innovation Award in the Advanced Mobility category.

A Safeway official said, “While we have been advancing our technology and preparing for overseas market entry, receiving an Innovation Award at a global stage like CES has generated strong interest from Unveiled attendees and given momentum to our business expansion,” adding, “We expect this to help raise awareness in the U.S. and Japanese markets, where demand for the Ascender platform and related technologies is high, and to increase the feasibility of local market entry.”

The official continued, “The United States and Japan are among the countries where aging trends are most pronounced, and demand for advanced personal mobility solutions that support mobility in diverse environments is expected to continue growing,” adding, “This presents an opportunity for our highly scalable technology to demonstrate its strengths, and we aim to lay the groundwork for globalization starting with these two markets.”

Meanwhile, the company will also participate in the main CES 2026 exhibition, held from January 6 to 9, as part of the Seoul Pavilion located in Eureka Park, the startup-dedicated exhibition zone. The CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion, led by the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), brings together 19 startup support organizations in Seoul, including district offices, related institutions, and universities, to support 70 startups. The participating companies span advanced technology fields such as AI, mobility, and healthcare, and selected outstanding firms receive opportunities to participate in the official CES media event, CES Unveiled.

‘CES Unveiled’ is a key official event held ahead of the CES opening, bringing together Innovation Award winners and companies showcasing innovative, cutting-edge products. The event brings together global media, company executives, government officials, and major technology industry stakeholders in one place.
